articles.title: Who is fifth and final member of Team USA for Survivor Series? Cody Rhodes and CM Punk find their pick on SmackDown
articles.summary: Trick Williams is the fifth and final member of Team USA for Survivor Series: WarGames.
articles.body: Trick Williams is the fifth and final member of Team USA for Survivor Series: WarGames. Cody Rhodes and CM Punk settled the spot on the November 20 SmackDown in Evansville, Indiana. Punk had first put forward Hacksaw Jim Duggan, Rhodes pushed back, and Duggan then said no himself. The United States Champion came out with Lil Yachty, made his own case, and got the nod. Team USA will face Rey Mysterio's Team Mexico on November 28 in Houston. The show ended with word backstage from Nick Aldis that Williams was hurt.Who is the fifth member of Team USA at Survivor Series?Trick Williams got the spot after a detour. Rhodes had told Aldis he would name the pick that night, but Rey Fenix then reported that Punk was already heading to the ring. Punk opened the segment by presenting Hall of Famer Hacksaw Jim Duggan as his pick, and Rhodes was not sold. They went back and forth until Rhodes gave in. A video package on Team Mexico then aired, and Duggan changed his mind. He asked if they still wanted him in the match, said no and left the ring.Williams came out next with Lil Yachty, with Rhodes and Punk still in the ring. Yachty argued the United States Champion deserved a place on Team USA, and the two leaders agreed. All four hugged. Duggan was the sentimental pick. Williams is the practical one, because a champion is a built-in argument.WWE announced the decision online soon after. "Team USA with the United States Champion?!" the post from @WWE said. It went on: "As agreed upon by @CodyRhodes and @CMPunk, @_trickwilliams is the 5th Member of Team USA for Survivor Series!"Team USA's lineup and the Priest attack on WilliamsWilliams then wrestled Damian Priest, with Yachty at ringside. Priest landed early right hands, but Williams answered with a neckbreaker and a clothesline that sent Priest over the top rope to the floor. Williams then threw Priest into the announce table. As Williams set up a big boot, Priest grabbed the ring bell and hit him with it. The referee called for the bell, and Williams won by disqualification.Priest was not done. He hit Williams again after the match, and WWE officials came out to pull them apart. Backstage, Aldis told Rhodes and Punk that Williams is hurt. Both were angry. How serious the injury is has not been made clear, and the spot is not safe until WWE says more.Team USA now has Rhodes, Punk, LA Knight, Je'Von Evans and Williams. Rey Mysterio's Team Mexico has Mysterio, Penta, Rey Fenix and Dragon Lee, with the fifth name still to come. Fenix was on the SmackDown card too, booked against Kit Wilson.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Harry Kane to miss ‘a few months’ after injury as Bayern Munich draw
articles.summary: Ballon d’Or winner tears a ligament in his left ankle during Bayern Munich’s 1-1 draw against Cologne.
articles.body:
England football captain Harry Kane will miss the “next few months” after tearing a ligament in his left ankle during Bayern Munich’s 1-1 draw against Cologne on Friday.

Kane was taken down in the area by Cologne defender Joel Schmied, who reached Michael Olise’s low cross first but knocked into the Ballon d’Or winner’s left leg in his follow-through at the back post.

Kane writhed in pain. Although he gingerly got back to his feet and initially continued playing, he soon hobbled off the field with two physiotherapists after treatment.

A club statement on X said: “Harry Kane suffered a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle in Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga home match against Köln on Friday evening. This was confirmed by an examination by Bayern Munich’s medical department. The 33-year-old will therefore be out for the next few months.”

Kane is the undisputed star of Bayern. Since joining from Spurs in 2023, he has scored 156 goals in 161 competitive fixtures and won two Bundesliga titles and the German Cup.

He became the first Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or in 25 years last month and, two weeks ago, signed a new contract with Bayern that will keep him in Bavaria until June 2029.

The night was supposed to be a happy one for Bayern, who welcomed coach Vincent Kompany back to the dugout a month after he collapsed while watching the reserve squad train.

However, Kompany saw his team go behind after just 11 minutes when winger Mikey Moore, on loan from Tottenham, started and finished a counterattack.

Just nine minutes later, Kane limped off to be replaced by Tom Bischof, and the German midfielder made a quick impact. Before halftime, he found Nathaniel Brown, who fired a fierce shot into the bottom corner from the edge of the box.

Both sides had chances in a busy second half but it remained goalless and the point was enough for Bayern to edge a point ahead of Borussia Dortmund. Bayern remained the only unbeaten team in Europe’s top five leagues.

Cologne, for which Moore was named man of the match, climbed one place into 14th.

articles.title: Villamanín vuelve a vender Lotería de Navidad un año después del Gordo que casi rompe el pueblo: "Hace pensar que hay tongo"
articles.standfirst: La comisión de fiestas que vendió participaciones anunció que volverá a jugar este año
articles.summary: La comisión de fiestas que vendió participaciones anunció que volverá a jugar este año
articles.body: Hace casi un año, Villamanín pasó de la euforia a la tensión. El Gordo de la Lotería de Navidad de 2025, el 79.432, dejó en esta localidad leonesa 35,6 millones de euros a través de las participaciones de la comisión de fiestas. Pero pronto se descubrió que 50 de esas papeletas, valoradas en unos cuatro millones, no estaban respaldadas por décimos tras el extravío de un talonario. El pueblo se dividió entre quienes disculpaban el error y quienes se planteaban denunciar. “Hace pensar que hay tongo”, llegaron a decir algunos vecinos. La reunión convocada por la comisión con los agraciados duró más de cuatro horas y estuvo marcada por los gritos e incluso crisis de ansiedad. La solución llegó con un acuerdo de quita para que todos los premiados pudieran cobrar. Los miembros de la comisión renunciaron a su parte del premio, más de dos millones de euros, y los pagos comenzaron en marzo. En abril, la asociación dio el proceso por prácticamente cerrado con un balance “muy positivo”, pese a dos intentos de estafa y una denuncia. Por el camino, comisiones de fiestas de toda España enviaron décimos de la Lotería del Niño en señal de solidaridad. La historia ha inspirado la serie documental ‘El Gordo de Villamanín’, de Movistar Plus, y terminó con un concierto gratuito de Carolina Durante en el pueblo. En junio, en su decimoquinto y último comunicado, la comisión dio una sorpresa: “Este año volveremos a vender Lotería de Navidad”. Lo hará a través de una nueva asociación, que también organizará los festejos. Sus integrantes habían asegurado en los peores momentos de la crisis que jamás volverían a hacerlo. Por ahora no han detallado si recurrirán de nuevo a las participaciones ni qué garantías adoptarán para evitar otro error.

articles.title: Bad news for Commanders regarding a Laremy Tunsil return in 2026
articles.summary: Don't expect the Commanders to get star left tackle Laremy Tunsil back this season.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders enter Monday's game against the Cincinnati Bengals at 3-5-1. Only recently has it looked like Washington has started to figure things out on both sides of the ball with new coordinators David Blough (offense) and Daronte Jones (defense).

Offensively, things began to unravel on Aug. 8, when star left tackle Laremy Tunsil tore his triceps during a training camp practice. Washington moved Brandon Coleman back to left tackle. Coleman was competing for a starting spot at left guard, so the injury affected two positions.

Tunsil, the NFL's highest-paid offensive lineman, has been around the team while he recovers from his injury. He looks fine. Of course, that means nothing, as he must pass a physical, and a triceps injury is often significant enough to be season-ending.

However, when head coach Dan Quinn spoke to the media this week, he offered an update on Tunsil.

"He had a good last visit, so during the Giants week, he had the next visit with the doctor, and they'll progress into the next phase, which is the beginning of the strength portion," Quinn said of Tunsil.

"So that's some good news. So, if you find yourself in the spots he expected them to be, I think that's good news. But as far as looking away, weeks from now, I think that's too early to call with the exception of good progress and doctors are pleased and ready to begin the next phase. So, I think anytime you're dealing with something, you get onto the next spot, then you're hitting the right things that you need to hit."

You can see why that update got some Washington fans excited, especially if the Commanders are in playoff contention next month.

Tashan Reed of The Washington Post revealed on Friday that Tunsil is not expected to return in 2026.

Reed said that while Tunsil was not expected to return in the regular season, he could play if the Commanders make the playoffs. However, overall, Tunsil's chances of a return are "very slim," Reed noted.

While that's not the news Washington fans wanted to hear, the chances of him returning after a triceps injury in the summer were minimal. It's a significant injury.

Coleman has had his moments in Tunsil's place. While the offensive line has been criticized for much of the season, the unit has played much better in recent weeks. They'll have their hands full with Dexter Lawrence, Jonathan Allen and the Bengals on Monday night.

articles.title: CCA girls sweep, Southern Lee wins two, Lee County splits wrestling matches
articles.summary: Local high school wrestling teams turned in strong performances Thursday night, with Central Carolina Academy’s girls sweeping two matches, Southern Lee winn...
articles.body:
Local high school wrestling teams turned in strong performances Thursday night, with Central Carolina Academy's girls sweeping two matches, Southern Lee winning twice and Lee County splitting its season-opening dual meets.

Central Carolina Academy, Southern Lee compete at Eastern Guilford

Central Carolina Academy traveled to Eastern Guilford for a quad meet featuring North Carolina Leadership Academy and Southern Lee.

The CCA girls dominated their competition, posting identical 18-6 victories over Southern Lee and North Carolina Leadership Academy.

Ryleigh Russell and Isabella Gonzalez led the Eagles, each finishing 2-0. Sydney Stewart and Daphnee Ballenger went 1-1 apiece to help secure the two victories.

On the boys' side, Central Carolina Academy continued to struggle with open weight classes, surrendering valuable team points through forfeits.

Despite the disadvantage, the Eagles battled Southern Lee before falling 36-30.

Charlie Wright led CCA with a perfect 3-0 record. Kevin Spivey Jr. (2-0) and Jean Marie Murry (1-0) also went undefeated, while Ty Couture finished 2-1.

Esau Martinez went 1-1, while Tyler Hunter and Eli Soto each finished 1-2.

Southern Lee finished the night 2-1, defeating Central Carolina Academy 36-30 and North Carolina Leadership Academy 53-24 before falling to Eastern Guilford 69-6.

Southern Lee will compete in the King/Queen Wake of the East tournament Friday and Saturday before hosting a tri-meet Monday.

Central Carolina Academy will travel to North Moore for a 6 p.m. match Tuesday.

Lee County splits season-opening dual meets

The Lee County Yellow Jackets opened their dual-meet season Thursday, Nov. 19, splitting matches against Cary and South Granville.

Lee County fell to Cary 60-24 before rebounding with a 30-23 victory over South Granville.

Against Cary, the Yellow Jackets recorded four victories, including two pins.

Beckham Glasson (144 pounds) pinned Nathaniel Rolon in 26 seconds, while Platon Horner (150) pinned Neil Devkota in 3 minutes, 12 seconds.

Alex Dell (175) and Jancarlo Espinosa (285) each earned victories by forfeit.

Lee County responded with a strong team effort against South Granville to secure its first dual-meet victory of the season.

Liam Kelly (132) pinned Massiah Paylor, while Dell (175) recorded his second victory of the night with a pin over Max Loera.

Kash Lett (157), Victor Rodriguez (190) and Braxton Tickle (215) each picked up victories by forfeit.

Yellow Jackets coach Anthony Dell praised his team's effort and development.

"We have a young team with a lot of potential, and nights like this are important for our development," Dell said. "We saw some things we need to improve, but we also saw our wrestlers compete, respond to adversity, and support one another. I'm proud of the effort and excited about where this team is headed."

Lee County will return to action Saturday, Nov. 21, at the Cecil J. Mock Invitational at Eastern Randolph High School.
authors: ZACK CIBOTH, The Sanford Herald, N.C.

articles.title: Bayern Munich star Harry Kane breaks silence with defiant hospital update after undergoing surgery on serious ankle injury
articles.summary: Harry Kane has provided a positive update for fans after successfully undergoing surgery on a serious ankle injury sustained during Friday’s Bundesliga actio...
articles.body:
Harry Kane has provided a positive update for fans after successfully undergoing surgery on a serious ankle injury sustained during Friday's Bundesliga action. The Bayern Munich striker faces a lengthy rehabilitation process away from the pitch following a major blow to the club's silverware ambitions.

The injury occurred during Friday night's 1-1 draw at home against FC Koln . Kane was forced off the pitch as early as the 20th minute after a collision with Joel Schmied. While attempting a shot in the penalty area, the England international was caught on the left foot by the defender's sliding challenge. Although there was no whistle from the referee or intervention from the VAR, Kane's attempt to play on was short-lived as the severity of the damage became clear.

The 33-year-old striker took to social media on Saturday morning to provide an update on his condition following the procedure. Posting a picture from his hospital bed with his left leg in a brace and both thumbs raised, the forward displayed a resilient attitude despite the significant setback. "The highs and lows of life!" Kane wrote on Instagram. "Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it's an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027. I'll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season!"

During the club's annual general meeting on Saturday, Bayern Munich president Herbert Hainer addressed the situation directly, expressing total confidence in the forward's recovery. He highlighted the mutual respect between the player and the club, noting that while Kane considers it an honour to play in Munich, the club feels the honour is actually theirs to have the World Player of the Year in their ranks.

he club's leadership are rallying around their star man, who has become the focal point of their attack since arriving from Tottenham Hotspur. "We are sure that you will come back even stronger," Hainer stated, as quoted by Sky Germany . "Harry Kane said when he was voted World Player of the Year that it is an honour to play for FC Bayern. The honour is not Harry's, it lies with FC Bayern."

Challenging times for the Munich hierarchy

The loss of Kane for several months represents a major blow to Bayern's silverware ambitions. Sporting director Max Eberl did not hide his frustration after the final whistle on Friday, describing the night as particularly painful for the squad. The injury crisis was further compounded by news that Michael Olise also suffered a foot contusion during the same match, though the French winger is expected to undergo treatment over the coming days rather than facing a long-term absence like his English teammate.

Eberl emphasised that while the situation is incredibly challenging, the team cannot afford to dwell on the misfortune and must find a way to adapt without their leading goalscorer. "This is not an easy situation at the moment. It is very challenging. The evening is very modest, it really hurts us extremely, but we can't lament too much now," Eberl admitted.

Kane now begins a rehabilitation process that will see him sidelined for a significant portion of the current campaign. With the injury involving the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle, the medical team will take a cautious approach to ensure stability before he returns to competitive action. Bayern will be forced to look for internal solutions to fill the void left by the England record goalscorer. As the club navigates a busy domestic and European schedule, the focus will remain on keeping their title hopes alive until Kane is "fresh and ready" to lead the line once again.

articles.title: Orlando Brown Jr says there’s something people don’t realise about Joe Burrow behind the scenes
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals offensive tackle Orlando Brown Jr thinks people don’t get to see just how hard Joe Burrow works and how obsessive he is behind the scenes....
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals offensive tackle Orlando Brown Jr thinks people don't get to see just how hard Joe Burrow works and how obsessive he is behind the scenes.

Burrow is in the middle of an MVP-level season, already notching 2,795 passing yards and 27 touchdowns to help the Bengals go 7-2.

Now, when speaking on Inside the Pocket with Orlando Brown Jr, his teammate has detailed just how much work the quarterback puts in behind the scenes, saying that work and his attention to detail is 'what makes him so great'.

Brown Jr said: "It's the work ethic of Joe Burrow that people are seeing. There's so much that people don't see. You don't see us on the aeroplane while everybody's sleeping and he's watching the tape, asking, 'Hey, man, what were you thinking here? What were you feeling? Hey, this is why I did this. Hey, next time…'

"People don't see that. 'Hey, right here, man, I thought you were going to run him on the field. If you can just…'

"People don't see that, bro. You know what I'm saying? And to me, that's what makes him so great: the work he puts in and his attention to detail."

Joe Burrow's work ethic hasn't changed in six years

Burrow was drafted to the Bengals in 2020 and even as a youngster, his work ethic behind the scenes was catching the eye of his coaches.

Brian Callahan was an offensive coordinator for Cincinnati six years ago and gave a glowing review of the quarterback at the time.

During an interview , he said: "His [Burrow's] offseason work was outstanding. He worked really hard. I think that part gets skipped over a little bit."

Even back then, the now 29-year-old's desire to work hard was having a positive impact on his teammates, with Callahan continuing: "He's such an intense worker. He's put himself in position to know what to do and how to do it. That has rubbed off on his teammates and obviously his presentation and how he goes about his business has been everything we had thought it would be."

Burrow and the rest of the Bengals are now gearing up to face the Washington Commanders on Monday. They have the joint-second-best record in the AFC ahead of the weekend's ties, one win behind the 8-1 Buffalo Bills.

articles.title: Prep talk: City Section, Southern Section cross-country finals are Saturday
articles.summary: Pierce College and Mt. San Antonio College will be the sites for high school cross-country championships this weekend.
articles.body:
The rain has stopped, which is perfect timing for the City Section and Southern Section cross-country finals to be held Saturday at Pierce College and Mt. SAC, respectively. Because of soaked ground conditions, Southern Section runners will use the rain course.

In the City Section, the Division I boys' race should feature a showdown between juniors Ethan Funk of Palisades and Miguel Mora of Carson. They finished one-two during last week's preliminaries.

Trabuco Hills, Redondo Union, Warren and Beckman all won heats in the team competition for the Southern Section Division 1 prelims. Ayden Ramirez of Cajon led the individuals with a time of 14 minutes, 22.8 seconds. For Division 1 girls, Corona Santiago is the team to beat.

Palisades is the heavy girls' favorite in City Section Division I. Emily Rodriguez of Granada Hills Kennedy had the fastest time in the prelims.

This is a daily look at the positive happenings in high school sports. To submit any news, please email eric.sondheimer@latimes.com.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: USC safety Prophet Brown set for final game at the Coliseum
articles.summary: After six years with the Trojans, safety Prophet Brown is set to play his final USC home game on Saturday.
articles.body:
This week, the USC football team will be back at the Coliseum to take on Maryland . It will be the final home game of the season for the Trojans , who are currently 7-3 on the year and 4-3 in Big Ten play.

In addition, it will mark the final home game for USC's 2026 senior class. One of those seniors is safety Prophet Brown, who has been with the program for a remarkable six years.

In a recent USC Athletics feature , Brown discussed his journey with the program.

"I've watched this program change and transition into what it is today, and it allowed me to see what it takes to create a winning team," Brown said. "That experience has been so great, and I have had so much fun learning throughout that process.

"I know it's rare to see someone in one place for so long, but I'm grateful to be so in love with this team. I hope to be remembered by my team as a caring guy who brought joy and positive energy to everyone in the facility, always with a smile on my face."

Kickoff between USC and Maryland is set for 3:15 p.m. Pacific time Saturday on Big Ten Network. Brown and the Trojans ' other seniors will be honored prior to the game.

articles.title: Arsenal Starting XI vs Newcastle United: Confirmed Team News and Predicted Lineup
articles.summary: Arsenal Team News: Bruno Guimaraes Set for St James’ Park ReturnBruno Guimaraes heading back to St James’ Park is the obvious storyline before Arsenal face N...
articles.body:
Arsenal Team News: Bruno Guimaraes Set for St James' Park Return

Bruno Guimaraes heading back to St James' Park is the obvious storyline before Arsenal face Newcastle on Saturday evening. He left Newcastle for Arsenal in a £75 million move this summer, and this will be his first return to the ground where he built his reputation over four and a half seasons.

There is no mystery about the reception Mikel Arteta wants for his midfielder. Asked whether Guimaraes would get a warm welcome, the Arsenal manager said: "Well I hope so. I think he was one of the main players there and I think he came to the club in a really important part when they had obviously a massive lift in terms of performance and what they have achieved all together, which was really impressive."

Bruno Guimaraes in Arsenal Midfield Spotlight

Sentiment aside, the real issue is selection. Guimaraes has not fully nailed down a regular place in Arteta's starting side, but Martin Zubimendi's hamstring injury changes the equation. Zubimendi is out for "a few weeks", which leaves Arteta weighing up Guimaraes or Myles Lewis-Skelly in midfield alongside Declan Rice.

This feels like a game made for experience. St James' Park is awkward for Arsenal, loud, aggressive and rarely forgiving. Guimaraes knows the ground, knows the mood and knows plenty of the players. That matters.

Arsenal Team News Before Newcastle Clash

Arsenal are still without Bukayo Saka, who is expected to miss another month with a quad problem. Max Dowman remains suspended. Beyond that, Arteta has close to a full squad.

At centre-back, William Saliba is pushing for a return after stepping up his fitness. Ezri Konsa has the shirt for now, and Arteta may prefer continuity here, particularly with Borussia Dortmund coming up in midweek. Giving Saliba controlled minutes in Europe may be the cleaner call.

Noni Madueke should keep his place after a strong run, while Kai Havertz may again be preferred to Viktor Gyokeres in attack.

Predicted Arsenal XI: David Raya, Jurriën Timber, Ezri Konsa, Gabriel Magalhães, Riccardo Calafiori, Declan Rice, Bruno Guimaraes, Noni Madueke, Martin Odegaard, Christos Tzolis, Kai Havertz.

Kick-off is 5:30pm GMT on Saturday, November 21 at St James' Park. For Arsenal, the main call is straightforward enough, trust Bruno Guimaraes in the one stadium where he will not need directions.

articles.title: Philadelphia mayor wants the Eagles to play in a dome
articles.summary: The Eagles will become an indoor team if the mayor of Philadelphia gets her way.
articles.body:
The Eagles will become an indoor team if the mayor of Philadelphia gets her way.

" I want a dome ," Mayor Charelle L. Parker said on 93.3 WMMR, via the Philadelphia Inquirer . "Don't you tell. This is a secret between us. I just saw a rendering of this beautiful dome that they're talking about for the Bears."

Moving into a dome would change the character of late-season and playoff games in Philadelphia, which are often affected by snow, wind and cold. Plenty of fans won't like it. But politicians and NFL owners often prefer stadiums with roofs because they bring in lucrative events, indoor sports, concerts, conventions and trade shows.

The Eagles told season ticket holders last year that they are looking at either renovations to Lincoln Financial Field or a new stadium . Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie has committed only to staying in "the region," not in the city of Philadelphia, but both Parker and Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro have said they want the Eagles to remain in the city.

The Eagles' lease at Lincoln Financial Field runs through the 2032 season.

articles.title: NHL trade rumors: Could Dylan Larkin's reported interest in Utah Mammoth lead to a major Detroit Red Wings trade
articles.summary: Explore the latest NHL trade rumors surrounding Dylan Larkin and his potential interest in joining the Utah Mammoth, and the implications for the Detroit Red Wings.
articles.body: According to NHL trade rumors, the Utah Mammoth have reportedly made contact with the Detroit Red Wings about a possible trade for captain Dylan Larkin. Larkin is said to be open to Utah, but the Mammoth may have second thoughts if Detroit holds firm on a hefty asking price.Pierre LeBrun of The Athletic said Utah has explored the possibility of trading for Larkin. Mammoth is interested, and it is noteworthy, as the forward is said to be interested in a move to any of the 10 teams that the franchise has on its list. But reported discussions don't mean a trade is necessarily imminent. The cost, both in dollars and players, to acquire Detroit’s captain may factor into Utah’s decision to move forward.Could Utah Mammoth acquire Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin?The Utah Mammoth have been identified as a potential trade landing spot for Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin, but the price tag is still a major sticking point.The Utah Jazz have continued to discuss the possibility of acquiring the veteran center from Detroit, according to LeBrun’s reporting. It’s reported that Larkin would be open to the destination, giving the Mammoth a big leg up in exploring a potential deal.Larkin’s availability would be a massive development for Utah. The 30-year-old forward has become a valuable offensive contributor and leader in Detroit, making him an appealing option for a franchise looking to bolster its roster.But Utah's reported interest should not be mistaken for a confirmed offer or agreement between the organizations. There seems to be a recurring theme in the discussions, which is the Mammoth’s view of the reasonableness of Detroit’s demands.The biggest obstacle appears to be the return expected from the Detroit Red Wings.Detroit would probably want a lot for their captain, especially with how much he means to the franchise. In dealing a player of Larkin’s caliber, the organization would have to consider not only where it sits competitively today, but what the roster will look like down the road.LeBrun’s report suggests Utah may have stayed involved partly because Detroit could eventually lower its demands.That could be an important detail. If the Red Wings work out, Utah may decide it can use its assets on the table for better use, whether it’s chasing another center or other roster needs.The Mammoth would be making a significant investment in Larkin, not just a routine roster move.How could Dylan Larkin change the Utah Mammoth roster?The Utah Mammoth could add a proven center in Dylan Larkin who can bring offensive production, leadership, and experience.The franchise has been trying to establish itself as a competitive force in the NHL. Add a proven Detroit Red Wings captain and it could strengthen its forward group while providing another key option down the middle.Larkin’s experience could also help younger players grow in a more competitive environment. As much as he’ll help on the ice, he’s an interesting prospect from a leadership standpoint, too.But Utah would have to consider the long-term cost of giving up a lot for one guy.The Detroit Red Wings would have some big decisions to make, as well. Trading their captain could indicate a major shift in the direction of the organization, while keeping him would keep an established leader that the team can continue to build around.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Where to watch Grand Slam of Curling National: Schedule, times, channels, live streams, scores for 2026
articles.summary: Teams Mouat and Homan will look to three-peat this week in Nova Scotia. Here's when and where to watch all the action.
articles.body:
The Grand Slam of Curling is back this week with the GSOC National in Sydney, Nova Scotia.

The third of five events in this year's series, the National features some intriguing lineup changes, including the first action this season for some high-profile Americans.

Five-time Olympian John Shuster won a qualifier to get into the field, and Milan Cortina 2026 mixed doubles silver medalist Korey Dropkin will step in as a sub for skip Matt Dunstone's side, which went unbeaten in winning the GSOC Masters two weeks ago.

While Dunstone and Isabel Wrana will look to make it two GSOC wins in a row, Bruce Mouat and Rachel Homan are two-time defending champions at the National.

Who will prevail this week in Nova Scotia? Here's all you need to know to watch all the action this week.

Where to watch Grand Slam of Curling National

Live streams: Fubo (Canada), Sportsnet+, Rock Channel , ESPN app

Fans can stream the entire Grand Slam of Curling National via Rock Channel, which will have exclusive live coverage of the morning draws each day, along with games not selected for featured spots on the main broadcast the rest of the day.

For viewers in Canada, one featured game during the afternoon and evening draws will air on Sportsnet channels and Sportsnet+ from Tuesday through Friday, along with Saturday's quarterfinals and Sunday's finals. The men's and women's semifinals will air on the CBC and Sportsnet+ and can also be streamed via Fubo .

Fans in the U.S. can stream the Grand Slam of Curling Masters via Rock Channel and ESPN+, which is available via the ESPN app . Each afternoon and evening draw will see a featured game spotlighted on the ESPN+ broadcast, with other games available on Rock Channel. All morning draws will stream exclusively on Rock Channel.

articles.title: Michigan State Spartan fans believe basketball team is still a top team
articles.summary: Spartan Fans not concerned about basketball team’s performance against Tennessee
articles.body:
It's Saturday, and that means the votes are in. Thank you for all of you who have been voting in these polls. Quick reminder that these surveys will appear in The Feed early in the week as well as in their own article, so you should have every opportunity to see it and participate. You must have a TOC account to vote.

Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android .

On Tuesday night, MSU Basketball lost to Tennessee. This was no ordinary loss, however. The Spartans put up a historically inept offensive performance, making only 9 FGs the entire game. The 18% on FGs was all-time MSU low. So was this a reason for a full-blown panic or was this a nothing-burger? Or maybe somewhere in the middle?

Nearly half of TOC Nation, 46%, believe there is no need to worry. Some of you pointed out in the comments that nagging injuries to Coen Carr and Jordan Scott kept MSU from playing to their potential, while many were adamant that the team will never shoot that bad again, and that even a few percentage points better could have turned the game in MSU's favor.

We will see how this plays out. Today's game should be an easy one but there are still a couple of major teams – Arkansas and Gonzaga on neutral courts – to contend with before we jump into conference play. Let's see how MSU bounces back from the Tennessee debacle.

This survey was sponsored by the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook .

articles.title: Barkov and Marchand Close to Return as Panthers Navigate Heavy Schedule
articles.summary: Relief is finally within reach for the Florida Panthers. After grinding through a punishing early-season travel slate without two of their top offensive cata...
articles.body:
Relief is finally within reach for the Florida Panthers . After grinding through a punishing early-season travel slate without two of their top offensive catalysts, captain Aleksander (Sasha) Barkov and veteran winger Brad Marchand are nearing the finish line of their respective recoveries. However Florida Hockey Now reports that Barkov will not return for Saturday's game and no word on Marchand

Both forwards have been sidelined with knee injuries since the opening week of the 2026-27 season—Barkov since October 1 against San Jose and Marchand since October 6 against Los Angeles . Following their return to team skates earlier this month, head coach Paul Maurice confirmed that both players have avoided setbacks and are scheduled for final medical evaluations during the team's off day on Friday.

Maurice indicated that they are very close to returning, with Barkov likely tracking slightly ahead due to his injury timeline. This timing aligns perfectly as the Panthers (12-8-3) navigate a homestand at Amerant Bank Arena after a grueling early-season road schedule. The reintegration of Barkov and Marchand—alongside Gadjovich's return to practice—energizes a roster that has heavily relied on depth pieces like Sam Reinhart , Sam Bennett , Anton Lundell , and the Tkachuk brothers .

As the Panthers look to bolster their lineup, the potential return of these key players could provide the spark needed to elevate their performance as they head deeper into the season. Full details on the schedule context and locker room reactions can be reviewed in the source material.The Panthers host the Buffalo Sabres Novemeber 21st at 6:00 p.m. ET. Live score updates can be viewed on Sportswire Miami

articles.title: Clutch overtime 2-point conversion keeps Lake Travis Cavaliers alive in UIL playoffs
articles.summary: Lake Travis used great special teams play and an overtime gamble to beat Cibolo Steele in the UIL high school football playoffs.
articles.body:
SAN MARCOS - There was no doubt for Hank Carter. Or Jason Carter. Or Westin Smith.

If Lake Travis scored a touchdown in overtime Friday, it was going for two and the win .

"Once they scored, we had made the decision that if we had the opportunity to end the game, we were going to try to end it," Cavs coach Hank Carter said.

On what was literally a win-or-go-home play, Lake Travis' gamble paid off.

Jason Carter hit a wide-open Smith in the back of the end zone to give the Cavs a 39-38 win over Cibolo Steele in a Class 6A Division I area-round playoff game at Rattler Stadium.

"We've been practicing that play for weeks now and we finally used it," Smith said. "In the huddle beforehand after they took the timeout, (offensive coordinator Tommy) Mangino was like, 'You ready to win this?' And I was like, 'I'm ready.'"

UIL overtime rules mirror NCAA rules, with each team starting its possession on the 25-yard line. Lake Travis won the extra-period coin toss and chose to be on defense.

Steele (9-2-1) quickly scored, and when Jason Carter - the head coach's son - ran onto the field, he knew the game would soon be over one way or another.

"Before the drive started, I asked my dad if we were going for two, and he said yes," Jason Carter said. "I loved it. I agreed with it. And we executed it just like I thought we would."

It took a monumental second-half effort by the Cavs just to force overtime.

Lake Travis trailed 28-14 at halftime and had allowed Knights running back Marshall Kenner to run for 219 yards and four touchdowns.

But the Cavs continued to excel on special teams (more on that later) clamped down on defense and did enough offensively to tie the game at 31-31.

Kenner, who ended with 301 yards rushing, scored his fifth TD to start overtime, then Lake Travis responded with Teddy Lofgren connecting with Luca Antoun for a 12-yard touchdown on a double pass.

"Steele was moving the ball. We were having a hard time tackling them. They were pushing us around, and we had two defensive starters out. The longer that thing went, I didn't think it was going to go great for us," Hank Carter said. "But I felt pretty good about going for it. We thought we were going to get a good look, and I was just kind of like, 'Here we go. This is our season.' And the kids got it done and we get to come back to work tomorrow."

With its offense struggling, Lake Travis' special teams and defense came up with big plays to keep it in the game.

Owen Aird's 53-yard interception return to the Steele 2-yard on the game's fifth play set up Lofgren's TD run the next play. And the Cavs' special teams produced or led to 17 points as Antoun returned a kickoff 92 yards for a touchdown, Nolan Atkins had a 65-yard kickoff return to the Knights 11 that led to another Lofgren rushing TD, and Hendrix Bryant recovered an onside kick that ultimately turned into a field goal.

The two teams met in the regular season but the game ended in a tie.

"I felt like the area that we needed to try to win by a wide margin was special teams," Hank Carter said. "Steele has a lot of dynamic players and is bigger than us. … We've been gradually getting better on special teams, and I thought if we were aggressive, we'd have some chances."

Though Antoun's kick return came in the first half, it was important as it came at a point when Steele had all the momentum and the Cavs' offense was struggling.

"I kind of slow-played it, found an opening, and the second that I saw the gap, I just shot it and was gone," Antoun said. "Special teams were a game changer tonight."

Lake Travis will play San Antonio Brennan in the regional semifinals Friday at Texas State. For Antoun and the Cavs, this playoff run has extra meaning.

"I love these guys, love these brothers," he said. "We've had the most adversity this year with our teammate ( Odin Hensley , who died before the season started), and so we know how to respond. We know how to fight back, and that's what we did tonight."

images.caption: The Lake Travis Cavaliers celebrate becoming Area Champions and advancing in the playoffs after beating Cibolo Steele in overtime at Rattler Stadium in San Marcos, Nov. 20, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman)
